title: Delicious Library, 2004
lede: A Mac cataloguing app that showed books, films, and games as photoreal covers on a wooden bookshelf.
summary: Photoreal media covers on a wooden shelf. Delicious Monster, 2004.

creator.name: Delicious Monster (Wil Shipley and Mike Matas)

made: First released November 2004; Delicious Library 2 in 2008

evidence.note: The archived 2009 website ([capture](ref:delicious-monster-website-2009)) shows a small screenshot of the shelves, too small to describe. Based on Wikipedia and TechCrunch (2010).

styles.note: A precursor on the Mac: the wooden bookshelf that iBooks later resembled.

context: Delicious Monster was founded by Wil Shipley and Mike Matas; Matas left in 2005 to work for Apple. Delicious Library won Apple Design Awards, including Best Mac OS X User Experience (2005). [Wikipedia: Delicious Monster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delicious_Monster).
The software was first released in November 2004; Delicious Library 2 was released in 2008. [Wikipedia: Delicious Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delicious_Library).

TechCrunch (27 January 2010): “the bookshelf view in iBooks is nearly identical to the main bookshelf view used in Delicious Library.” [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2010/01/27/think-ibooks-looks-familiar-youre-not-the-only-one/).
interpretation: The link from this app to [iBooks](ref:ibooks-ipad-2010) through one designer shows how the style moved from independent Mac software into Apple’s own apps.

rights.statement: Delicious Monster software; copyrighted. No image is stored here.
